newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - FINANCIAL TIMES JUNE 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - FINANCIAL TIMES JUNE 5.

-- AMERICAN AIRLINES HINTS AT DEAL TO SECURE BA ALLIANCE

American Airlines has improved its standing with the US congress by agreeing to a congressional report suggesting that other US carriers be given more slots at Heathrow Airport in London. The positive reaction to the report could lead to congress taking an easier stance towards the possible British Airways and American alliance, which would be one of the most powerful in aviation history, carrying more than 60 percent of traffic between the US and UK.
-- HARRODS FORMS LINK TO DEVELOP RIVERSIDE SITE

UK retail group Harrods has teamed up with executive homes developer Berkeley Homes in a project to develop Harrods 10- acre landmark depository building that overlooks the Thames at Barnes. Berkely have reportedly paid Harrods 30 million stg for the property, and the retailer may share some of the profits from the 180-million stg project that involves 250 luxury apartments and townhouses.
-- FARMERS CALL FOR GREEN POUND REDRESS

Britain's farmers' leaders are set to renew demands for government compensation for the strength of the sterling against other European currencies. Due to the strength of the sterling, the green pound -- the rate at which EU payments and subsidies are converted from the Ecu into sterling -- underwent a near three percent revaluation on Wednesday, causing a drop in support payments and thus cutting farm profits.
-- MINISTER BACKS COMPETITION IN POWER SECTOR

UK Energy Minister John Battle declared on Wednesday that the Labour government remains committed to competition in the power sector, but requires that the competition 'benefits the many and not the few'. Battle also said that it must be ensured that energy supplies are used sustainably and do not prejudice the prospects of future generations'.
-- $10BN LOAN DEAL FOR BT, MCI

British Telecommunications and MCI of the US have attained a $10 billion syndicated market loan to fund the launch of their global telecoms alliance, Concert. The loan will cost them 0.1 percentage points over Libor, the rate at which banks in London lend to one another. London bankers said the loan is the latest in a series of the compression of margins in a market where the borrower is in control.
-- BRITISH ENERGY MAKES FIRST PROFITS IN SHARP TURNAROUND

UK privatised nuclear facility British Energy has announced pre-tax profits of 61 million stg and turnover up 13 percent to 1.87 billion stg for the year to March, backed by strong performances by its eight power stations. British Energy has also secured a long-term, 1.5 billion stg agreement with British Nuclear Fuels to reprocess waste fuel, which it estimates will add 10 million stg a year to pre-tax profits.
-- BT CHIEF SET FOR BONUS WINDFALL

It has been estimated that British Telecom chief executive Peter Bonfield may receive pay of up to one million stg in addition to existing bonuses and incentive payments from the planned merger with MCI in each of the next two years as a result of bonus schemes detailed in the company's annual report. Shareholders in the telecoms company will be asked to approve the bonuses at the annual meeting on July 16
-- SOUTHERN 'CAN WITHSTAND LEVY'

British electricity firm Southern Electric's finance Director Ian Marchant has suggested that his company has the 'balance sheet strength' to withstand the windfall tax and return funds to shareholders. Analysts have predicted that if the government is looking to raise five billion stg through the windfall tax, Southern will have to pay about 100 million stg.
-- VIGLEN FIVE SET FOR FURTHER 10M STG

Five founding shareholders in Vieglen, the personal computer subsidiary of Amstrad that will float on the stock market in August, will receive an additional 10 million stg to complete an earn-out agreement that has netted them 60 million stg over three years. Alan Sugar, the former president of Amstrad, said the agreement would restrict Amstrad's ability to invest in Viglen, but that production levels at the PC company would see a 'dramatic increase'.
-- LYNX IN KALAMAZOO TALKS

Lynx Holdings, the acquisitive computer services group, has said it is in talks to take over the Kalamazoo computer group, but that talks are 'at a very early stage' and it remained possible that no bid would emerge from the talks. Lynx said the biggest problem facing the takeover was Kalamazoo Trust, the fund holding 40 percent of Kalamazoo shares -- which it may not be permitted to sell to anyone.
